summary: Large evening 5xx spike caused by accept-queue oscillation and runtime 'hot-sleep' stalls under mixed webhook fanout
description: Issue summary: Starting ~18:10 UTC on 2026-03-13 we saw a rapid elevation in 5xx responses for a subset of routes serving QueryStream Inc. traffic. Errors concentrated on streaming/chat and webhook fanout routes. The elevation correlated with an evening traffic pulse and repeated accept-queue collapse events on several API gateway nodes. Impact: Customer-facing errors (502/503/504) for QueryStream's dedicated pool; degraded throughput and multiple user sessions dropped. Some long-lived streaming sessions failed with partial zero-byte responses. Timeline: 18:08 - first small error uptick; 18:10 - steep rise in 5xx across multiple nodes; 18:15 - initial mitigation (priority-shed) applied; 18:22 - runtime restart observed on 3/8 dedicated instances; 18:30 - temporary drop in errors but recurrence at 19:05. Environment: Dedicated Redwood pool for QueryStream in prod-us-east with autoscaler configured to min 4 / max 16 GPUs. Mixed workload: short webhook fanouts + long-lived streaming chats. Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay customer's webhook-fanout pattern from their load simulation (fanout size ~12, many short-lived connections). 2) Mix in long-lived streaming sessions (keepalive interval ~60s). 3) Apply sharp concurrency ramp to mimic evening pulse. Observed behavior: API gateway accept-queue depth increases then oscillates, causing connection drops and hedged-retry amplification. Upstream runtimes enter a hot-sleep state where a subset of worker threads appear idle but CPU and GPU memory remain pinned, leading to failing healthchecks and eventual process restarts. Expected behavior: graceful queueing with backpressure and autoscaler warmup without inducing runtime panic or repeat restarts. Initial workaround applied: temporarily scaled dedicated pool to max + enabled stricter ingress rate-limiting for QueryStream routes to reduce fanout concurrency. This reduced immediate error rate but did not eliminate recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: Run customer traffic pattern with webhook fanout size ~12 and short timeouts
Simultaneously open ~50 long-lived streaming sessions with keepalive 60s
Observe API gateway accept-queue depth and upstream 5xx rate

comments: Support (Aisha): Received alert from QueryStream at 18:11 UTC reporting 502 spikes. Added to customer status channel #support-qs and notified on-call SRE.

SRE (Diego): Investigating accept-queue growth and runtime health. Observed repeated small restarts on runtimes pinned to the dedicated pool. Temporarily increased pool size and toggled ingress rate limits for the customer routes.
Customer (J. Huang - QueryStream): We saw many client errors and reconnect loops. Will provide traffic replay script (incoming) and confirm fanout sizes.
Eng (L. Kim): Looking at possible prioritizer mis-evaluation when short-lived fanouts dominate accept queue; also suspect stale keepalive handling in runtime that prevents worker reuse (hot-sleep).
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: accept_queue_depth spiked exactly when webhook fanout ramped; apigw backpressure propagated hedged retries which amplified upstream load
Heap/GC: Runtimes show increased GC pause percent > 40% on node-3 during the spike; pause timeline aligns with worker idle periods in logs
Hypothesis 1: Accept-queue oscillation causes bursts of hedged retries which overwhelm runtime scheduler leading to hot-sleep where threads hold device memory but are not scheduling inference tasks
Hypothesis 2: A recent prioritizer patch (PR #4921) regresses scheduling fairness for mixed short/long workloads; under fanout-heavy traffic short tasks starve long sessions and then induce retries
Evidence: PR #4921 touches the priority window logic and test matrix shows mixed workload flakiness on staging under synthetic fanout
Repro: Local load replay reproduced accept-queue oscillation and produced similar runtime 'idle but pinned memory' traces within 2-3 minutes
resolution: Temporary: Applied stricter per-route concurrency caps and disabled hedged-retry for affected webhook endpoints for QueryStream; scaled dedicated pool to +4 nodes to give headroom. Medium-term: rollback the prioritizer change from PR #4921 in the dedicated pool and add a small scheduling backoff for short-lived fanout requests to prevent accept-queue oscillation. Long-term: add a runtime health probe to detect 'hot-sleep' states (threads idle + pinned device memory) and trigger graceful worker recycling before kernel/driver resets. Rollout notes: Rollback of prioritizer change staged to 2 nodes at 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC in prod-us-east; monitoring alerts created for accept_queue_depth and runtime_pinned_memory_ratio. Follow-ups: implement canary test that simulates mixed webhook+streaming traffic for every prioritizer change; add runbook steps for rapid temporary concurrency capping for customers during evening pulses.
